articles.title: De-dollarization: The End of Dollar Dominance?
articles.dek: Top dollar no more? Discover the factors threatening the dominance of the world’s reserve currency and how this is playing out across markets.
points: While the U.S.’s share of global trade has declined, the dollar’s transactional dominance is still evident in areas including FX volumes and trade invoicing.
While there are currently no scalable alternatives to the dollar, China is settling more trades in yuan, while BRICS nations are exploring a common currency to reduce their dependence on the dollar.
Currently, the dollar-centric system gives the U.S. significant geopolitical leverage beyond cheaper funding costs, including the ability to impose sanctions and control payment systems.

articles.title: The Institute Employment Report: August 2026
articles.dek: Growth in jobs and after-tax wages softened in August, but both continue to suggest a broadly resilient labor market.
points: Bank of America customer deposit account data suggests labor market momentum cooled in August, with estimated payroll growth of 1.5% year-over-year (YoY), down from 1.8% in July.

The long-standing "K" shape between higher- and lower-income households' after-tax wage growth has reversed: August saw lower-income households' after-tax wage growth of 4.7% YoY, while higher-income households' after-tax wage growth was 3.5% YoY.

Recently, there has been an increase in job switching, and the pay change associated with a job change reached the highest level in more than three years in July. This acceleration is most notable among weekly-paid employees, suggesting rising mobility among hourly and lower-income workers may be contributing to the narrowing of wage growth differences.

articles.title: Volatility is no longer the exception
articles.dek: Geopolitical shocks, commodity swings, retail flows, and rapid reversals are changing how markets move. Explore how institutional traders are managing volatility as an ongoing condition—using data, technology, and judgment to respond faster and think further ahead.
points: Volatility, now considered a defining feature of today’s markets, is forcing investors to rethink how they manage risk, build resilience, and target opportunities.
Geopolitical fragmentation, commodity disruption, and retail participation are making market moves faster, sharper, and harder to read.

Technology is helping traders process information and respond more efficiently to changing market conditions, while advances in execution tools, data, and analytics are reshaping how risk is monitored and managed.

articles.title: Restaurants: What’s cooking in consumer spending?
articles.dek: A restaurant rebound is taking shape, powered by stronger wage growth, Gen Z spending and independent eateries.
points: Americans are dining out again, according to Bank of America card data. Restaurant spending and transaction growth have both improved meaningfully in 2026. Some consumer food spend also appears to be shifting from grocery stores to restaurants, helped by easing restaurant inflation, trade-offs in the grocery space, and faster after-tax wage growth than a year ago.

The restaurant recovery is being led by younger and lower-income consumers, supported by improving wage growth, according to Bank of America internal data. Lower-income households are now posting the fastest restaurant spending growth among income groups, while Gen Z leads all generations by a wide margin.

Consumers are favoring local restaurants over large chains, according to Bank of America card data. Despite accelerating restaurant spending, some national chains are not fully participating in the rebound. Spending growth appears strongest at independent restaurants, regional operators and other non-chain establishments.

articles.title: Metals Outlook: Price Forecasts for Copper, Steel and Aluminum
articles.dek: From tariffs to capex to geopolitics, what are the forces shaping the industrial metals market?
points: J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts the price of copper to reach $14,800/metric ton (mt) in the fourth quarter of this year, driven by sulfur shortages, tight mine supply, an industrial boom and the threat of U.S. tariffs.

The price of aluminum is forecasted to reach $3,800 per metric ton in the third quarter of 2026, and $3,700 in the fourth quarter, based on supply disruptions arising from the Middle East conflict and possible shifts in Chinese export policy.
The price of steel remains highly region-dependent, with tariffs keeping prices elevated in the U.S. and EU, while China’s property slump has driven prices down.

articles.title: Silver Price Forecast for 2026 and 2027
articles.dek: With tightness unwinding and rate hikes on the horizon, silver prices face an uncertain future.
points: J.P. Morgan Global Research forecasts the price of silver will reach $63 per ounce in the fourth quarter (Q4) of 2026, averaging $70/oz for the year and $63/oz in 2027.
This transition has also pushed the gold-to-silver price ratio back to more traditional levels, in which gold dominates.
Along with taking cues from gold, silver’s price path could be determined by the direction of interest rates, with a hike likely dampening the appeal of precious metals.

articles.title: The AI-Driven Memory Shortage: DRAM Prices, Inflation and Market Risks
articles.dek: The latest bottleneck in AI expansion is memory chip and DRAM storage, with knock-on effects in inflation and national security.
points: AI data center construction and hyperscaler demand are absorbing a disproportionate share of global memory capacity, creating a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) shortage that may take years to unwind.
J.P. Morgan Global Research estimates that DRAM prices will have risen more than 400% from the start of 2024 to the end of 2026.
The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for software and accessories and Producer Price Index (PPI) for storage devices have both risen 23% since the end of 2024.

The memory supply crunch is also straining cybersecurity infrastructure, with analysts warning that a major cyberattack could unleash an estimated $145 billion in additional chip demand on an already constrained market.

articles.title: ETF Market Guide: Understanding the $22 Trillion Industry
articles.dek: ETFs continue to grow in scale and complexity, with total assets under management up 43% year over year as of April 2026. What are their benefits, and how are regional ETF markets performing?
points: ETFs offer investors various benefits, including portfolio diversification, intraday liquidity and lower costs compared with mutual funds.
Total ETF assets under management (AUM) amounted to around $22.1 trillion globally as of end-April 2026.
Active ETF products continue to scale rapidly, representing more than 60% of new launches in each of the past six years.
